description: Solo team from Visakhapatnam building “Still Here”, an interactive storytelling app for school-age space fans about NASA machines left on the Moon and Mars. Each machine sends “On this day” messages, and you can search NASA pictures and explore their stories. Challenge: Abandoned but not Forgotten.
summary: Still Here is a storytelling app where NASA machines left on the Moon and Mars send “On this day” messages. Students explore their stories and NASA pictures, and learn why each went quiet.
details:
Still Here is an interactive field atlas about 11 machines that NASA left on the Moon and Mars, built for the challenge “Abandoned but not Forgotten”. Students can browse the traces left on the Moon and Mars, filter them by world and mission state, search by machine name, and read a short sourced record with a real NASA image for each one. A daily “On this day” card appears when a recorded mission event matches today’s date. A flight-log panel shows that Ingenuity was planned for up to five flights and completed 72.

Every fact links to a NASA source. Details we could not verify are marked “unknown”, and where NASA pages disagree (the landing dates of Surveyor 3 and Opportunity) both sourced dates are kept instead of choosing one. The app is available in English, Spanish and Hindi, with English as the original, and a “Listen to summary” button reads text aloud using the browser’s built-in voice. It is one self-contained HTML file with the images embedded, so it works offline once downloaded.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no server or database. Built with AI assistance (code and text). Images are real NASA images with credits.

How to open Still Here

  1. Google Drive’s preview cannot run the app. Click Download and save the file or zip.
  2. If it is a zip, extract it fully first (Windows: right-click, Extract All. Mac: double-click).
  3. Double-click index.html. It opens in Chrome, Edge or Firefox. No install, command or internet is needed, except to open the NASA source links.
  4. Use the Language menu at the top right to switch language. “Listen to summary” depends on voices installed on the device, and a Hindi or Spanish voice may be missing.
